briefs.attachment: 46 s video: a Longbow drives down a ramp, anchors, shells an enemy base, walks on its siege legs, packs up and fires on the move; top-down, first and third person; day into night; ends pulling out to the gas giant.
facts: The Longbow is a tank that anchors into artillery.
Every shot is the real game, staged and recorded hidden by an agent skill at a fixed 30 fps, with the game's own sound.

briefs.attachment: GIF: the camera pans across a base at dusk.
facts: Nine days old: started 28 September 2026.
Claude Code wrote all the code, about 96,000 lines of C++. The developer hasn't written any of it by hand.
Grok and Gemini painted the concept art; agents built the 3D models from it. Suno made the music, ElevenLabs the voices and sound effects.
Known rough edges, in the developer's notes: the sky high up is too blue, and the third-person shots still look rough.
All of it is public domain (CC0).

briefs.attachment: 6 s GIF: the camera dives from the top-down RTS view into a Ranger, who walks out in first person.
facts: Click any of your units and the camera dives in, 1.2 s from the top-down view to the unit's own eyes.
From there you play it like a shooter: WASD walks, the mouse aims, a click fires. Esc hands it back to the AI commander.

briefs.attachment: Screenshot: two upgrade cards over the Prospector's cockpit at a level-up.
facts: The more you play a kind of unit yourself in a match, the better every unit of that kind gets.
Each level offers two upgrade cards and you keep one: 216 upgrades across the twelve kinds.
This card: 'Every Prospector pumps MH 20% faster.' The Prospector is the worker that mines and builds.
It gives you a reason to play the dull units yourself, the worker first.

briefs.video: record: the base at dusk with a KSTR ad playing, sound on
briefs.attachment: 20 s clip with sound: an in-game radio ad over the base at dusk.
facts: The game's music plays as a radio station, KSTR 88.7 Stardust, with fake ads between songs for the world's products.
The songs are made with Suno; the ads are voiced with ElevenLabs.
The developer votes songs and ads up or down in the game's player, which also logs how long each is heard; the next batch is written from what worked.
Thinking about adding podcast segments about the world's lore.

briefs.attachment: Three images: the Atlas walker's concept painting, its six-view turnaround sheet, the model in the engine.
facts: Each unit starts as a concept painting from Grok.
The picked one becomes a six-view turnaround sheet.
A Claude Code agent builds the model part by part in Unreal's Geometry Script, procedurally, and fits it against the six views.

briefs.attachment: The Longbow video, recorded by the new path.
facts: An agent skill records staged moments of the real game, hidden, at a fixed 30 fps with the game's sound.
saw: a 10 s clip took about 7 minutes to record, every frame saved as a PNG then encoded.
did: the agent reads frames back from the GPU asynchronously and pipes them raw into ffmpeg while the game runs.
now: about 25 s per 10 s clip.
felt: the developer asked 'why does it take 7 minutes to record?' and 'if I run the game at 60fps, why can't it record at 60fps?'

briefs.attachment: Screenshot: the top-down view of a base, the Citadel and its ore line.
facts: The whole game is public domain under CC0: code, art, 3D models, sounds, music, docs.
Use any of it for anything, no credit needed.
The repo also holds the Claude Code skills the agents work from.

briefs.attachment: Screenshot: the command map, the bases of the map and the team's objectives.
facts: Your team's AI commander runs the army, so you don't micromanage.
Press M for the command map: set a stance and objectives (attack, defend, hold), and the AI plans the rest.

briefs.attachment: 8 s GIF: playing a Comet in first person, jumping up a cliff.
facts: The Comet is a jump-pack raider with twin pistols.
It clears cliffs other ground units must walk around.
Comet Jump Academy, an ad on the game's radio: most graduates land.

briefs.attachment: Screenshot: the base at night, beacons and lamps lit.
facts: The sun crosses the sky in every match; at night the beacons and lamps come on.
A gas giant hangs over the map, Ashfall Reach.

briefs.video: record: the old Swift wallpaper next to the Unreal game today
briefs.attachment: Two images: the old Swift live-wallpaper version and the Unreal game today.
facts: The game began on 28 September as a Mac live wallpaper in Swift and SceneKit: the AIs played on the desktop background.
SceneKit choked at about 150 units, and the game wants eight-player battles with big armies.
On 4 October the developer chose Unreal Engine 5; Claude Code agents ported the simulation line by line to plain C++ and rebuilt the game in Unreal in about two days.
The Swift version was retired on 5 October.

briefs.attachment: GIF: a Prospector drilling Stardust Ore in first person.
facts: The Prospector is the worker: mines Stardust Ore, pumps Metallic Hydrogen, builds, repairs.
You can take one over and mine by hand in first person.
Stardust Ore: dark rock with opal shimmers that shift teal, violet and gold with the view angle.

briefs.video: record: a screen capture of an agent recording a clip while the developer works
briefs.attachment: Screen capture: an agent's terminal recording a game clip while the developer keeps working in another window.
facts: Every game run an agent starts is hidden and silent: a copy of the editor with no Dock icon, rendering offscreen, its sound written to a file.
So agents test the game and record clips on the developer's Mac while the developer keeps using it.
Every clip and GIF in the repo was recorded this way by the video skill.

briefs.attachment: Screenshot: the Atlas heavy assault walker, from its cockpit.
facts: The Atlas is a heavy assault walker, one of the newest units.
An agent built its model procedurally in Geometry Script from a six-view turnaround sheet.
Like every unit, you can take it over and play it.

briefs.attachment: 8 s GIF: two armies of twelve meet in the desert, seen from above as the camera sweeps in.
facts: Two armies of twelve, staged by the game and recorded at a fixed 30 fps.
Matches have up to eight players fighting over ore deposits.

briefs.attachment: The Longbow video, made by the video skill.
facts: The Claude Code skills the agents work from are in the repo: concept art to Unreal model, the buildings' light language, testing, video.
This video was staged, recorded and cut by the video skill.
CC0: copy them into your own project.

briefs.video: record: the base under attack with the Oracle's warning, sound on
briefs.attachment: 10 s clip with sound: the base voice warns that the base is under attack.
facts: The base voice is called the Oracle. Its warnings never say its name.
Oracle Premium, an ad on the game's radio: forty voices and smooth jazz while the base burns.
Voiced with ElevenLabs.

briefs.video: record: a close-up of a Metallic Hydrogen well
briefs.attachment: Close-up: a pool of mirror-silver liquid metal in a rock mound.
facts: Metallic Hydrogen, the second resource: a liquid metal like mercury.
It sits in wells: silver liquid that heaves slowly, cold blue-white light at the rim, pale vapour boiling off.
A Derrick is built over a well to pump it.
Quicksilver Cola, an ad on the game's radio, is pumped from these wells. Not a beverage.

briefs.attachment: GIF: a Ranger walking in third person.
facts: Press V to switch the unit you're playing between first and third person.
The Ranger is the rifle infantry.
